introduction: On this Sunday, two widows give everything they have. The widow of Zarephath shares her last handful of flour with Elijah, and her jar does not run empty. In the Gospel, Jesus watches a poor widow put two small coins in the temple treasury and says she has given more than all the others. The Letter to the Hebrews tells us that Christ offered himself once for all. Let us learn generosity from those who give from their poverty.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord upholds the widow and the orphan. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may be a community where the gifts of the poor are honored and their needs are met. Let us pray to the Lord.
For widows, widowers and all who live alone: that they may be cared for and never forgotten. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who give generously in hidden ways: that God, who sees in secret, may reward them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For leaders, in the Church and in the world: that they may never take advantage of the weak. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may give to God and to others not only from our surplus but from our hearts. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you see the gift of the poor widow and you never fail those who trust in you. Make us generous with all we have, and bring us to your Kingdom. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: All that she had
reflection.body:
In a time of drought and famine, Elijah meets a widow gathering sticks at the gate of Zarephath. He asks for water and a piece of bread. She tells him the truth: she has only "a handful of meal in a jar and a little oil in a jar," and she is about to make a last meal for herself and her son, "that we may eat it, and die." Elijah asks her to make him a little cake first, and promises that God will provide. She trusts and gives, and "The jar of meal didn't run out and the jar of oil didn't fail."

In the Gospel, Jesus first warns against religious leaders who love long robes and places of honor and who "devour widows' houses." Then he sits opposite the temple treasury and watches people put in their offerings. Many rich people put in large sums. Then "A poor widow came and she cast in two small brass coins."

Jesus calls his disciples to notice her: "this poor widow gave more than all those who are giving into the treasury, for they all gave out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, gave all that she had to live on." God does not measure gifts by their size but by the love and trust behind them.

The Letter to the Hebrews reminds us that Jesus himself gave everything. He offered himself "once at the end of the ages... to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself." The widow's two coins are a small image of that total gift.

These widows challenge us. We often give what we can spare. This week, think about how you give: to the Church, to the poor, of your time and attention. Choose one gift that costs you something, and offer it with trust that God will provide.
